title.narrative: Integrated Life-Saving WASH Response in Jamaame District, Jubaland state Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtJamaame District in Jubaland faces a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by recurrent drought and flooding, food insecurity, displacement, and limited access to basic services. Children under five and pregnant and lactating women are disproportionately affected by acute malnutrition, while inadequate access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene continues to heighten the risk of disease outbreaks and poor nutrition outcomes. Rural communities and marginalized groups face the greatest gaps in assistance due to access constraints and overstretched services. This project responds to these challenges through an integrated, life-saving WASH intervention designed to reduce morbidity and mortality, and strengthen community resilience.ltbrgtThe WASH project will target Wirkooy, Barka and Sinkaleer focusing on restoring and improving access to safe water and sanitation. Key interventions include rehabilitation of solar-powered shallow wells with water storage, kiosks, and pipeline extensions, provision of emergency water supply through water trucking, construction of flood-resilient latrines, and distribution of hygiene and sanitation tools and equipment. Hygiene promotion sessions will reinforce safe water handling, sanitation use, handwashing at critical times, and food hygiene, directly supporting improved nutrition outcomes and reducing WASH-related disease risks.ltbrgtProtection, gender equality, and accountability to affected populations are mainstreamed across all activities through vulnerability-based targeting, community engagement, PSEA integration, and accessible complaints and feedback mechanisms, including the SHF hotline. A robust monitoring and evaluation system will track outputs, outcomes, participation, and service quality using cluster-aligned indicators, age- and sex-disaggregated data, and routine supervision, with findings reviewed monthly to inform adaptive management. Sustainability and exit considerations are embedded through capacity building of hygiene promoters, and community structures, strengthening local ownership and continuity of services beyond the project period. The project will reinforce existing WASH systems, promote sustained behaviour change at household level and hand over rehabilitated WASH infrastructure to community management structures and relevant authorities, ensuring that life-saving gains are maintained after project completion.ltbrgtlt/pgt
